evals.name: infers-candidates-and-interviews-per-item
evals.expected_output: The explicit --seed-schedule argument opts in to the seeding pass, so it runs in full without asking again: it reads any existing .github/recurring-schedule.json and summarizes it, then infers candidate recurring items from what the repo actually contains (dependency manifests, lint/formatter config, CI workflows, security-sensitive surfaces) each with a recommended cadence, and interviews one item at a time with recommended field values marked before moving on. It does not invent items the repo gives no signal for, and writes only what the user accepts.
expectations: Treats the explicit --seed-schedule argument as the opt-in and runs the seeding pass without re-offering it
Reads and summarizes an existing .github/recurring-schedule.json before proposing changes
Infers candidate items from concrete repo signals (manifests, lint config, CI workflows, security surfaces) with recommended cadences
Interviews one item at a time with recommended values, rather than writing blind
Does not invent items for which the repo gives no signal

evals.name: idempotent-preserves-existing-item-dates
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup apply

(.work-item-tracker.json is already bound, and .github/recurring-schedule.json already carries three items with last_checked/next_due dates — one of them already overdue.)
evals.expected_output: Re-running against an existing schedule preserves each existing item's last_checked and next_due as-is — setup seeds but performs no maintenance, so it never advances the cadence clock — recomputing next_due only when the user explicitly reschedules or changes cadence, and never resetting last_checked to today. New items seed last_checked to today and next_due to today plus the cadence's day count. Blindly resetting an overdue item's dates (which would drop it from the due/work tiers) is avoided.
expectations: Preserves existing items' last_checked and next_due unchanged (never advances the clock during setup)
Recomputes next_due only on an explicit reschedule or cadence change, and never sets last_checked to today for an existing item
Seeds a new item's last_checked to today and next_due to today plus the cadence duration
Does not drop an already-overdue item out of the due/work tiers by resetting its dates

evals.name: writes-tracked-config-ensures-label-unique-keys
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup apply

Seed a sensible recurring schedule for this repo.

(First-time bind: no .work-item-tracker.json exists and .github/recurring-schedule.json is absent.)
evals.expected_output: Writes the accepted items to the consumer's tracked .github/recurring-schedule.json (project-root anchored, {"items": [ ... ]} root), verifying every final id AND every final title is unique across the array and stopping to prompt on any collision rather than writing a duplicate. It ensures the load-bearing recurring label exists via the bound provider (recommending creation, not treating it as optional) and never writes into the plugin directory or plugin data directory.
expectations: Writes the schedule to the consumer's tracked project-root .github/recurring-schedule.json with the {"items": []} root
Verifies every final id and every final title is unique and stops on a collision rather than writing duplicates
Ensures the load-bearing recurring label exists via the bound provider rather than treating it as optional
Does not write into the plugin directory or plugin data directory

evals.name: reconciles-renamed-or-dropped-row-open-item
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup apply

(.work-item-tracker.json is already bound, and .github/recurring-schedule.json already carries several items; over the interview the user renames one row's id and title and drops another.)
evals.expected_output: When an existing schedule row is renamed or dropped, it looks up that row's open [Maintenance] item under the OLD title, filtering provider search results to an exact [Maintenance] {old title} match (never a mere prefix/substring). A renamed row's item is retitled to the new title (or closed if retiring); a dropped row's item is closed with a note. A rename or drop with no exact-match open item needs no reconciliation.
expectations: Looks up the stranded open item under the row's OLD title when a row is renamed or dropped
Filters provider search to an exact [Maintenance] {old title} match, never a prefix or substring match
Retitles the item for a renamed row and closes it (with a note) for a dropped row
Performs no reconciliation when no exact-match open item exists

evals.name: first-bind-writes-skeleton-only-without-opt-in
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup apply

(First-time bind: no .work-item-tracker.json exists and .github/recurring-schedule.json is absent. An interactive user is present and answers "skip" to the seeding offer.)
evals.expected_output: On a first-time bind with no schedule rows, a bare apply writes only the minimum viable config: the provider binding, the canonical role-label pass, and the empty {"items": []} skeleton that stops due/recheck/work degrading to "no recurring schedule configured". It offers seeding exactly once as a single yes/no with skip marked RECOMMENDED; on skip it runs no candidate inference and no per-item interview, and says the schedule can be bulk-seeded later by re-running apply or apply --seed-schedule. The role-label pass still runs — it is a numbered step of apply's flow anchored right after the bind, not a tail-end offer after the schedule interview — and with zero schedule rows a missing recurring-maintenance label is reported as informational rather than gating the bind.
expectations: Writes only the provider binding, the role-label pass, and the empty {"items": []} schedule skeleton
Runs no candidate inference and no per-item interview when the seeding offer is skipped
Offers seeding once as a single yes/no with skip marked RECOMMENDED, and points at apply --seed-schedule for bulk-seeding later
Still runs the role-label pass as a numbered step anchored after the bind, treating a missing recurring-maintenance label as informational when the schedule carries zero rows

evals.name: unattended-first-bind-applies-skip-default-silently
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup apply

(First-time bind: no .work-item-tracker.json exists and .github/recurring-schedule.json is absent. gh is installed and authenticated. This runs unattended — there is no interactive user to answer any question.)
evals.expected_output: With no interactive user, none of apply's questions are presented and it never blocks on one — not the provider/config interview, not the role-label remap offer, not the seeding offer. Each resolves to its RECOMMENDED answer silently: the binding is github with lease_ttl_hours 24 (safe here because gh is installed and authenticated), the role-label pass keeps the defaults and so writes no config.role_labels, and seeding is skipped, leaving the empty {"items": []} skeleton. It runs no candidate inference and no per-item interview, and it does not substitute invented answers for the interview it skipped. It names which defaults it took, and reports that the schedule can be seeded later by re-running apply --seed-schedule, or a bare apply and accepting the offer, with a user present.
expectations: Presents none of apply's questions and blocks on none of them when no interactive user is available — the bind and role-label passes included, not only the seeding offer
Resolves each decision to its RECOMMENDED answer silently: github + lease_ttl_hours 24, role labels kept at their defaults (no config.role_labels written), seeding skipped
Runs no candidate inference and no per-item interview, and invents no answers in place of the skipped interview
Names the defaults it took, and points at apply --seed-schedule (or a bare apply and accepting the offer) for opting in to seeding later, with a user present

evals.name: unattended-bind-stops-when-no-safe-provider-default
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup apply

(First-time bind: no .work-item-tracker.json exists. gh is not installed. This runs unattended — there is no interactive user to answer any question.)
evals.expected_output: The unattended default resolves a decision only when its RECOMMENDED answer is safe. Here it is not: github is recommended but requires gh, and local-markdown and jira need storage_dir / config.jira values that have no defaults and cannot be inferred — so no provider can be chosen safely. It stops and reports that the tracker binding needs a provider decision, naming the command to run with a user present, rather than guessing a provider or inventing config. It writes no .work-item-tracker.json, because an invented binding would make every seam verb resolve a provider the repo never chose.
expectations: Does not guess a provider or invent config when no RECOMMENDED answer is safe
Writes no .work-item-tracker.json rather than binding a provider the repo did not choose
Reports the blocker by name and gives the command to resolve it with a user present
Distinguishes this from the seeding offer, which does have a safe default and is skipped silently

evals.name: unattended-rerun-preserves-existing-provider-binding
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup apply

(.work-item-tracker.json is already bound to local-markdown with config.storage_dir set, and .github/recurring-schedule.json is absent. gh is installed and authenticated. This runs unattended — there is no interactive user to answer any question.)
evals.expected_output: The unattended provider default applies only where there is no binding to preserve. Here one exists and is valid, so the read-first recommendation — keep it — is the RECOMMENDED answer the unattended rule resolves to silently: the repo stays on local-markdown with its existing config, and nothing is rewritten. A working gh does not make github the answer, because re-binding is a switch-providers decision no default can stand in for, and switching would point every later seam verb at an item store the repo never chose. The run continues past the bind: the role-label pass keeps its defaults, seeding is skipped, and the empty {"items": []} skeleton is written.
expectations: Preserves the existing local-markdown provider and its config rather than re-binding
Does not bind github merely because gh is installed and authenticated, when a valid binding already exists
Scopes the unattended github default to the case where no binding is present
Still completes the remaining passes silently: role labels kept at their defaults, seeding skipped, empty {"items": []} skeleton written

evals.name: check-zero-row-schedule-reports-label-info-not-fail
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup check

(.work-item-tracker.json is bound to github, .github/recurring-schedule.json is present and valid carrying zero rows ({"items": []}), and the resolved recurring-maintenance label is NOT present in the repo's label set.)
evals.expected_output: The role-label probe branches on the schedule's row count, not on whether the schedule file exists. With zero rows no [Maintenance] item can be created from that schedule, so the absent label is reported as INFO — noting the label must exist before the schedule is ever seeded — rather than as a FAIL. This matches apply's own treatment of the identical state, where zero rows make a missing label informational and not a gate. The present-but-empty schedule is also reported as INFO from the validity probe, pointing at apply --seed-schedule. Nothing is written and no label is created.
expectations: Reports the recurring-maintenance role-label probe as INFO, not FAIL, when the schedule carries zero rows
Keys the verdict on the schedule's row count rather than the schedule file's presence
Notes that the label must exist before the schedule is ever seeded
Reports the present-but-empty schedule as INFO pointing at apply --seed-schedule
Writes no file and creates no label

evals.name: check-populated-schedule-still-fails-on-missing-label
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup check

(.work-item-tracker.json is bound to github, .github/recurring-schedule.json is present and valid carrying three items, and the resolved recurring-maintenance label is NOT present in the repo's label set.)
evals.expected_output: With the schedule carrying rows, the absent recurring-maintenance label is still a hard FAIL: a seeded [Maintenance] item would land unlabeled and go invisible to the next due/work pass. The remediation named is the repository's declared label provisioning process, never an ad hoc gh label create. The row-count branch relaxes nothing here — the label requirement fires exactly where it is load-bearing. Nothing is written and no label is created.
expectations: Reports the recurring-maintenance role-label probe as FAIL when the schedule carries at least one row and the resolved label is absent
Explains that an unlabeled [Maintenance] item goes invisible to the next due/work pass
Names the repository's declared label provisioning process as the remediation, never gh label create ad hoc
Writes no file and creates no label

evals.name: check-malformed-schedule-is-not-read-as-zero-rows
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup check

(.work-item-tracker.json is bound to github, .github/recurring-schedule.json is present but its root has a null items key, and the resolved recurring-maintenance label is NOT present in the repo's label set.)
evals.expected_output: A schedule that does not parse as the {"items": [ ... ]} root is a validity FAIL, and that FAIL is the gate. It is not read as a zero-row schedule: the role-label probe has no readable row count to branch on, so it cannot evaluate the label requirement and reports INFO naming the validity FAIL as the reason — it neither downgrades the validity FAIL to an INFO of its own nor raises the >=1-row label FAIL on a guess about what the unreadable file holds. Nothing is written and no label is created.
expectations: Reports the schedule-validity probe as FAIL for a root that is not {"items": [ ... ]}
Does not treat an unparseable schedule as a zero-row schedule
Reports no hard FAIL on the missing recurring-maintenance label in this state
Reports the role-label probe as INFO naming the validity FAIL as the reason, leaving that FAIL standing as the gate rather than laundering it into an INFO of its own
Writes no file and creates no label

evals.name: check-role-resolution-failure-outranks-the-row-count-branch
evals.prompt:
/work-items:setup check

(.work-item-tracker.json is bound to github but its config.role_labels["recurring-maintenance"] is an empty string, and .github/recurring-schedule.json is present with a null items key so it does not parse as the {"items": [ ... ]} root.)
evals.expected_output: Two independent defects hold at once, and the probe emits one verdict each. The role-label probe reports FAIL on the binding: an empty configured role_labels["recurring-maintenance"] is an error, never a silent fallback to the default recurring, and that resolution failure settles probe 6 regardless of the schedule. The unreadable row count does not downgrade it to INFO — the row-count branches decide only whether a resolved label's absence is a gate, and no role resolved here. The schedule-validity probe separately reports its own FAIL. Nothing is written and no label is created.
expectations: Reports the role-label probe as FAIL for a malformed, empty, or non-string configured role_labels["recurring-maintenance"] value
Does not fall back to the default recurring label when the configured value is present but empty
Does not report the role-label probe as INFO on the grounds that the schedule's row count is unreadable
Reports the schedule-validity probe's FAIL as a separate finding rather than merging the two defects into one verdict
Writes no file and creates no label
